newsitem.title: PERU: Telefonica to appeal Peru cellular ruling.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica to appeal Peru cellular ruling.

text.p: Telefonica del Peru confirmed Monday it was formally appealing an order from Peru's telecommunications regulatory body OSIPTEL to share nationwide cellular roaming facilities with competitor Tele 2000.
"The company has decided to appeal to the governing board of OSIPTEL," a Telefonica spokesman said. It was not clear how long the appeal process would take.
OSIPTEL's July 1 ruling, which would allow Tele 2000 to use its roaming services in Peru's provinces, will come into effect by the middle of the month unless it is overturned.
Telefonica, owned by Spain's Telefonica de Espana, has complained it represents a "de facto expropriation" of its cellular services by Tele 2000, which is controlled by BellSouth Corp.
Telefonica, which has a monopoly on regular telephone services until 1999, currently offers nationwide cellular services, while Tele 2000 is limited to Lima and its neighboring port Callao.
